guarantees.claim: For each share index i in [0, NumShares-1], msg_masked[i] is the bitwise XOR of msg[i] and the signal ({sha3_pkg::MsgWidth{msg_mask_en_i}} & msg_mask_permuted). Thus, when msg_mask_en_i is 1, msg_masked[i] = msg[i] ^ msg_mask_permuted; when 0, msg_masked[i] = msg[i].

assumptions.claim: Arrays msg and msg_masked are sized exactly NumShares elements deep, each element has width equal to sha3_pkg::MsgWidth, and NumShares is at least 1.
assumptions.risk: Out-of-bounds indexing or width mismatch would produce corrupt data or synthesis errors.

assumptions.claim: msg_mask_permuted is an independent, high-entropy masking value (e.g., from a cryptographic PRNG or permutation) that is uncorrelated with msg inputs.
assumptions.risk: Predictable or correlated mask would allow side-channel leakage of message shares.

assumptions.claim: msg_mask_en_i is a stable control signal that correctly reflects the security policy for masking; its assertion/deassertion is managed by external logic.
assumptions.risk: Incorrect assertion may leave critical data unmasked in a security-sensitive context, exposing secrets.

uncertain_points.claim: The source and entropy quality of msg_mask_permuted are not visible in this chunk; if the generator is weak or predictable, masking effectiveness is compromised.
uncertain_points.risk: Insufficient entropy leads to side-channel leakage of the message share through power or timing analysis.

uncertain_points.claim: Transitions on msg_mask_en_i relative to msg changes may cause a brief unmasked window if the control signal glitches or is not synchronized to data stability.
uncertain_points.cond: during transitions of msg_mask_en_i while msg is valid
uncertain_points.risk: Temporary exposure of unmasked msg data could occur before masking is re-established.
